messages:
jordan (CS): FYI customer reported weird rerank scores — some negatives and some >1, and they expected probabilities. Paste of their response below.

jordan (CS): customer quote: \"we're seeing scores like [-0.37, 0.12, 1.8] from /v1/rerank and they don't add to 1. Is this a bug? Which one is 'best'?\" :thinking_face:

jordan (CS): Repro they gave (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" 
 -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
 -d '{\n  "input": "Which restaurant near me has vegan options?",\n  "candidates": ["Joe's Pizza", "Green Bowl Cafe", "Thai Orchid"]\n}'
```

jordan (CS): Response they pasted:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood/rerank-small",
  "scores": [-0.37, 0.12, 1.8],
  "ranked_indices": [2,1,0]
}
```

jordan (CS): They expected floats in [0,1] or something normalized. Asking whether our rerank endpoint changed semantics.

maya (ML): short answer: not a bug. Rerank returns raw model scores (logits-ish), not probabilities. Negative values and >1 are both valid. We do not normalize by default because clients sometimes want raw scores for downstream combos.

maya (ML): longer: scores are model output activations before softmax. They can be negative or >1. To get probabilities do a softmax across candidates. Example (JS):
```js
function softmax(arr){
  const max = Math.max(...arr);
  const exps = arr.map(x => Math.exp(x - max)); // numerical stable
  const sum = exps.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0);
  return exps.map(e=>e/sum);
}
softmax([-0.37,0.12,1.8]); // -> [0.048, 0.131, 0.821] approx
```

maya (ML): Key guidance to share: 1) Rank by score (higher is better). 2) If you need probabilities, softmax client-side. 3) Scores are not comparable across models or prompt changes without calibration.

alex (eng): Thanks Maya. Docs call this out in the model pages but not the rerank API top-level doc. I'll open an issue to add a quick note and small example snippet. Also adding a small FAQ blurb on: "Why are scores negative? why don't they sum to 1?" :memo:

alex (eng): Filed INF-3247 to add examples + softmax snippet. Also tagging eng-ml to review wording.

priya (CS): Can we draft a short canned reply for the customer? They want to know what to do now. Prefer one that includes a ready-to-run snippet.

maya (ML): Suggest this reply: "Scores from /v1/rerank are raw model scores. Higher = better. If you need probabilities, apply softmax to the scores (example attached). If you're comparing across different model versions or prompt formulations, let us know; we can help calibrate or use our rerank-normalize feature (coming soon)."

priya (CS): Perfect. I'll send that + the JS snippet. Also asked customer whether they want normalized probabilities or just rankings.

rerank-bot: Auto-check: request payload size OK, model redwood/rerank-small within expected limits, latency 280ms on sample.

jordan (CS): Customer replied: they mostly just want to display a confidence % to end-users. Asking if we recommend softmax or some other calibration.

maya (ML): Softmax is fine for per-query normalization; caveat: softmax probabilities are sensitive to score spread. If they want calibrated probabilities across queries, recommend Platt scaling or isotonic calibration using a held-out labeled set. We can help if they share a small eval set.

alex (eng): Follow-ups: 1) Add softmax example to rerank API doc. 2) Add small FAQ entry. 3) Track feature request about server-side normalize param (feature ticket INF-3248 created).

priya (CS): Action: I'll reply to customer with the canned copy + softmax snippet and ask if they'd like help with calibration.

jordan (CS): Closing loop here — will post the customer reply once sent. :white_check_mark:
